label: desktop-report
title: Looking Glass · Gate 11 results
text:
LOOKING GLASS · GATE 11 · CLOSED EVIDENCE
Break a summary by changing its receiver
Pass · Bounded software and browser evidence

The count summary becomes insufficient when its receiver also requires calibration and custody authorization. Adding those two dependencies repairs it across all four fictional worlds. The actual browser completed the change, witness inspection, repair and reevaluation.

Run G11-RECEIVER-002 · build g11-7ced826c903d40c5a0dd
Source 7ced826c903d40c5a0dd6398477debdf65e1ccbd4a9260d4d0fe9556aad1fc70

Open paused instrument
All replay identities and restart commands
Primary-source review

This is a public software benchmark. All worlds and answers are inspectable. There were zero human participants; human omission detection, repair ability, learning and any diagram advantage remain untested. Gate 10's separate negative result is preserved unchanged.

2 fields
Unique global minimum in the declared menu
100 / 100
Complete snapshot hashes and layout checks
24.005 s
Actual natural tour, seven scheduled events
A different question needs different evidence

Every world has four amber field scanners. The initial summary contains the count and identical logical source references. That is enough to answer “Are there at least four scanners?” The release receiver also requires current calibration and approved custody authorization.

World	Calibration	Authorization	Count answer	Full-source release answer
W00	Expired	Pending	Yes	No
W01	Expired	Approved	Yes	No
W10	Current	Pending	Yes	No
W11	Current	Approved	Yes	Yes

Identical summaries now correspond to different release answers. A sound receiver reports insufficient information. Silently reusing the old “yes” would be wrong in three worlds.

A concrete collision. W10 and W11 share a baseline payload. The screenshot shows the separate provenance envelope and upper witness panel; complete pair values and different source answers were checked in the full DOM and exported records. Reading the whole capped panel requires internal scrolling.
The smallest repair in this menu

The menu allows calibration, authorization and paint color. All eight subsets were checked. Neither no repair nor paint alone helps. Calibration alone leaves W10/W11 unresolved; authorization alone leaves W01/W11 unresolved. Both dependencies suffice. Adding paint as well is redundant.

Calibration plus authorization is the unique globally minimal repair, with two menu entries. This minimum applies only to these four worlds and this menu. It is not a universal minimum, shortest encoding or claim that every individual decision needs both fields.

Actual local repair L1. The selected W11 receiver answers yes; the global panel reports no conflicting pair. The six typed relations identify the supplied dependencies and their source records.
The same evidence in plain form. Receiver result, global certificate and six relations agree with the diagram, with the same information hash. The test establishes data parity, not a preferred layout.
A local “no” can coexist with global insufficiency

One verified negative dependency is enough to reject release under this AND rule. Calibration-only W00 therefore determines no, although calibration-only summaries still fail to distinguish W10 from W11. The interface keeps the selected payload's answer separate from sufficiency across the entire family.

The negative control stays visible. Expired calibration determines no while authorization is absent. The global certificate remains insufficient. This untouched 960 × 720 capture shows wrapped controls without horizontal overflow.
What passed, and its boundary
Question	Observed	Boundary
Actual critical workflow	Receiver change → insufficiency → witness → two-field repair → reevaluation; both representations checked.	Source-informed software actions, not human detection or repair.
Provenance and isolation	Seven local revisions retain parents, copied source fields, hashes and actual repair events.	Full-source inspection remains outside the receiver's input; all data are public.
State and layout	All 100 semantic, information and receiver-payload hashes recompute; all 100 layout measurements match.	The earlier transport-limited capture is not complete hash evidence.
Replay	18 exact paused comparisons and a natural 24.005-second stop with seven events.	No separate active DOM capture during seconds 12–16; that boundary is recorded in events and a checkpoint.
Human outcomes	Zero participants.	Understanding, learning, omission detection and visual advantage remain untested.

The receiver accepts only the declared summary and receiver ID. World IDs, full-source hashes and revision identities sit in a separate inspection envelope. Opening full source does not improve the receiver's input. Only an explicit repair copies selected fields into it; source records remain unchanged.

Watch the saved demonstration
Click Reopen saved start, then Play.
At 4 seconds the receiver changes; at 8 seconds its collision witness opens.
At 12 seconds one positive dependency is still insufficient. At 16 seconds both dependencies determine the result.
At 20 seconds the plain representation shows the same information. At 24 seconds the initial display returns and the tour stops paused.

These are scripted events. Local controls create separately attributed revisions. The complete acquisition ends paused at zero; local history was exported before reload and was absent in the next document.

Preserved failures and capture limits

Candidate 001 completed the actual critical workflow, but an independent controlled reproduction found that a paused layout refresh could supersede a pending semantic publication. Candidate 002 corrected that race and passed the same reproduction. Both immutable candidates remain available; the finding is not presented as a host-observed on-screen failure.

The first candidate 002 acquisition completed the workflow but its structured tool output truncated 21 semantic and 66 information payloads and changed one active cursor by one ULP. The unchanged build was reacquired with lossless JSON text. One oversized read then failed after a successful export; its recorded capture error was followed by a read-only chunked capture. No incomplete record was silently rewritten.

The accepted complete pass contains 100 observations, 79 host actions and six originals. Including the failed candidate and earlier limited acquisition, the preserved totals are 276 observations, 221 actions and 17 instrument originals. The two complete-pass document exports are honest 56- and 21-event prefixes. All 1,437 historical frozen entries remain unchanged. Scrolling is needed for lower panels; no operating-system reduced-motion setting or human layout preference was tested.

Twelve preserved local replays

Each historical gate retains its own findings and qualifications. These are previews on this Mac and may need restarting; the collection above records exact commands.

Gate 0 · Viewing and replay
Gate 1 · 3D-to-2D calibration
Gate 2 · Hopf and shared reference
Gate 3 · 4D projection
Gate 4 · Slices and ambiguity
Gate 5 · Two additional coordinates in 5D
Gate 6 · Connected local models
Gate 7 · Unfamiliar-case interpretation and the bounded conclusion
Gate 8 · Indistinguishable worlds and revealing observations
Gate 9 · Choose, watch, or inspect a static sheet
Gate 10 · Predict an unseen view and transfer — prediction UI blocked
Gate 11 · Break a summary by changing its receiver
Stop before Gate 12

Gate 12 — Coordinate without erasing disagreement remains unapproved and unrun. Its proposed scope is a small shared decision that preserves explicit local references, incompatible judgments and an inspectable joint action. Human coordination claims would require actual authorized participants.

Astra specified and synthesized; Luna gathered primary sources; separate Sol workers implemented and audited. The host operated the browser and preserved originals. This page reports the closed core and independent pass. Final presentation verification, gate freeze, worker shutdown and publication are separate host records.

The receiver accepts only the declared summary and receiver ID. World IDs, full-source hashes and revision identities sit in a separate inspection envelope. Opening full source does not improve the receiver's input. Only an explicit repair copies selected fields into it; source records remain unchanged.

Preserved failures and capture limits

Candidate 001 completed the actual critical workflow, but an independent controlled reproduction found that a paused layout refresh could supersede a pending semantic publication. Candidate 002 corrected that race and passed the same reproduction. Both immutable candidates remain available; the finding is not presented as a host-observed on-screen failure.

The first candidate 002 acquisition completed the workflow but its structured tool output truncated 21 semantic and 66 information payloads and changed one active cursor by one ULP. The unchanged build was reacquired with lossless JSON text. One oversized read then failed after a successful export; its recorded capture error was followed by a read-only chunked capture. No incomplete record was silently rewritten.

The accepted complete pass contains 100 observations, 79 host actions and six originals. Including the failed candidate and earlier limited acquisition, the preserved totals are 276 observations, 221 actions and 17 instrument originals. The two complete-pass document exports are honest 56- and 21-event prefixes. All 1,437 historical frozen entries remain unchanged. Scrolling is needed for lower panels; no operating-system reduced-motion setting or human layout preference was tested.

Gate 12 — Coordinate without erasing disagreement remains unapproved and unrun. Its proposed scope is a small shared decision that preserves explicit local references, incompatible judgments and an inspectable joint action. Human coordination claims would require actual authorized participants.
